question: In March 2024, who among the following was elected as the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) president?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Devendra Jhajharia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In March 2024, ace para-athlete Devendra Jhajharia was elected unopposed as the President of the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) (भारतीय पैरालंपिक समिति के अध्यक्ष).

• He is a two-time Paralympic gold medallist in the men's javelin throw (F46 category), winning at Athens 2004 and Rio 2016.

• He is the first Indian para-athlete to receive the Padma Bhushan (2022) and was earlier awarded the Padma Shri and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The PCI is the apex national body governing Paralympic sports in India, affiliated to the International Paralympic Committee (IPC).

• Devendra Jhajharia hails from Churu district, Rajasthan.

NOTE

• Anil Kumar Prakash (Option 2): A sports administrator; not the elected PCI president in March 2024.

• Sundar Singh Gurjar (Option 3): An Indian para-javelin thrower and Paralympic medallist, not the PCI president.

• Mariyappan Thangavelu (Option 4): Paralympic gold-medal-winning high jumper (Rio 2016), an athlete and not the elected president.

question: In November 2024, Hemant Soren took oath as Chief Minister of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2024, Hemant Soren took oath as the Chief Minister of Jharkhand (झारखंड के मुख्यमंत्री) after the JMM-led alliance won the state assembly elections.

• He is a leader of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) and the son of JMM founder Shibu Soren.

• This marked one of his successive terms as Chief Minister of the state.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000; its capital is Ranchi.

• The 2024 Jharkhand Assembly election was won by the INDIA bloc led by the JMM.

NOTE

• Chhattisgarh (Option 1): Its Chief Minister (2024) was Vishnu Deo Sai of the BJP.

• Telangana (Option 3): Its Chief Minister was A. Revanth Reddy of the Congress.

• Rajasthan (Option 4): Its Chief Minister was Bhajan Lal Sharma of the BJP.

question: In June 2025, who took over as the 18th Commander-in-Chief of the Andaman and Nicobar Command?
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>Admiral R. Hari Kumar
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lt Gen Dinesh Singh Rana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2025, Lt Gen Dinesh Singh Rana took over as the 18th Commander-in-Chief of the Andaman and Nicobar Command (CINCAN) (अंडमान और निकोबार कमान के 18वें कमांडर-इन-चीफ).

• The Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC) is India's only tri-service (unified) theatre command, headquartered at Port Blair (Sri Vijaya Puram).

• He succeeded Lt Gen Ajai Singh in the post.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The ANC was established in 2001 and integrates the Army, Navy and Air Force under a single commander.

• The CINCAN reports to the Chief of Defence Staff / Chairman Chiefs of Staff Committee.

NOTE

• Lt Gen Ajai Singh (Option 1): The 17th CINCAN, whom Lt Gen Rana succeeded.

• Lt Gen Anil Chauhan (Option 3): Serving as the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of India, not CINCAN.

• Admiral R. Hari Kumar (Option 4): A former Chief of the Naval Staff, not the CINCAN.

question: Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) campaign September 2024 was observed from 17th September to 2nd October received participation from over _____ crore people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2024 campaign (स्वच्छता ही सेवा अभियान) was observed from 17th September to 2nd October 2024.

• It received participation from over 30 crore people across the country.

• The 2024 theme was 'Swabhaav Swachhata, Sanskaar Swachhata', marking a decade of the Swachh Bharat Mission.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• SHS is an annual pre-Gandhi Jayanti fortnight of mass cleanliness drives under the Swachh Bharat Mission.

• The campaign concludes on 2nd October, observed as Swachh Bharat Diwas and Gandhi Jayanti.

NOTE

• 50 (Option 2): Not the reported participation figure for SHS 2024.

• 100 (Option 3): An overstated figure; not the official number.

• 5 (Option 4): Far too low to reflect the nationwide participation of the campaign.

question: The Union Budget 2025-26 announced to set up a Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence for education with a total outlay of Rs _____ crores.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 500.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Union Budget 2025-26 announced a Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence for education (शिक्षा के लिए आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस में उत्कृष्टता केंद्र) with a total outlay of Rs 500 crore.

• It builds on three earlier AI Centres of Excellence set up in agriculture, health and sustainable cities.

• The 2025-26 Budget was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2025.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Budget also proposed 10,000 fellowships for technological research in IITs and IISc under the PM Research Fellowship scheme.

• AI Centres of Excellence aim to promote research, skilling and innovation.

NOTE

• 200 (Option 1): Not the announced outlay for the AI-in-education Centre of Excellence.

• 100 (Option 2): Incorrect figure for this scheme.

• 300 (Option 3): Incorrect figure; the correct outlay is Rs 500 crore.

question: Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana approved in July 2025 aims to benefit how many (in crores) farmers initially?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.7.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (प्रधानमंत्री धन-धान्य कृषि योजना), approved by the Union Cabinet in July 2025, aims to benefit about 1.7 crore farmers initially.

• The scheme targets 100 districts with low agricultural productivity, low cropping intensity and limited credit access.

• It has an annual outlay of about Rs 24,000 crore and runs for six years (from 2025-26).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The scheme converges 36 existing schemes across 11 departments, inspired by the Aspirational Districts Programme model.

• It focuses on crop diversification, irrigation, storage and easier access to credit.

NOTE

• 2.5 (Option 2): Not the initial beneficiary figure announced for the scheme.

• 1.2 (Option 3): Incorrect; the target is 1.7 crore farmers.

• 2.0 (Option 4): Incorrect figure for the initial beneficiaries.

question: Namo Drone Didi is a central sector scheme aiming to empower _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is women-led Self-Help Groups.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Namo Drone Didi is a central sector scheme aiming to empower women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) (महिलाओं के नेतृत्व वाले स्वयं सहायता समूह).

• It provides drones to women SHGs so they can offer drone-based agricultural services such as spraying fertilizers and pesticides on a rental basis.

• The scheme aims to make rural women 'Drone Pilots' and generate additional income of the SHGs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The scheme is linked with the Lakhpati Didi initiative and the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM).

• It targets equipping thousands of women SHGs with drones over its implementation period.

NOTE

• men-led Self-Help Groups (Option 2): The scheme is exclusively for women SHGs, not men.

• corporate-led Self-Help Groups (Option 3): SHGs are grassroots community groups, not corporate bodies.

• foreign companies'-led Self-Help Groups (Option 4): The scheme targets Indian rural women's groups, not foreign companies.

question: By how much the Reserve Bank of India's Financial Inclusion Index has improved from FY 2024 to FY 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.8%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Reserve Bank of India's Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index) (भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक का वित्तीय समावेशन सूचकांक) improved by about 2.8% from FY 2024 to FY 2025.

• The index rose from 64.2 (March 2024) to 67.0 (March 2025), an increase of 2.8 points.

• The FI-Index captures the extent of financial inclusion on a scale of 0 to 100, where 0 means complete exclusion and 100 means full inclusion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The FI-Index has three broad parameters: Access (35%), Usage (45%) and Quality (20%).

• It was first introduced by the RBI in 2021 and is published annually.

NOTE

• 3.8% (Option 2): Overstates the year-on-year improvement in the FI-Index.

• 5.8% (Option 3): Incorrect; the actual improvement was 2.8 points.

• 4.8% (Option 4): Not the reported change in the index.

question: District Hospital Index published by NITI Aayog is based on how many Key Performance Indicators?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The District Hospital Index published by NITI Aayog (नीति आयोग का जिला अस्पताल सूचकांक) is based on 10 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

• The indicators assess the performance of district hospitals in areas such as bed occupancy, human resources, diagnostics and service delivery.

• The assessment helps identify best practices and gaps in the functioning of district hospitals across India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• NITI Aayog released a report on 'Best Practices in the Performance of District Hospitals' based on this assessment.

• A key benchmark used is the WHO-recommended norm of 22 beds per 1,00,000 population.

NOTE

• 4 (Option 1): Too few; the index uses 10 KPIs.

• 5 (Option 2): Incorrect number of performance indicators.

• 7 (Option 3): Not the number of KPIs on which the index is based.

question: In March 2025, the 7th meeting of the National Board for Wildlife held at _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gir National Park.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In March 2025, the 7th meeting of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) (राष्ट्रीय वन्यजीव बोर्ड की 7वीं बैठक) was held at Gir National Park (Sasan Gir), Gujarat.

• The meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the occasion of World Wildlife Day (3 March).

• Gir is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica) in the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The National Board for Wildlife is the apex body for wildlife conservation, chaired by the Prime Minister.

• During the visit, the PM also launched initiatives related to lion conservation (Project Lion).

NOTE

• Manas National Park (Option 1): A UNESCO World Heritage Site and tiger reserve in Assam, not the venue.

• Kanha National Park (Option 3): A famous tiger reserve in Madhya Pradesh, not the meeting venue.

• Silent Valley National Park (Option 4): An evergreen tropical forest park in Kerala, not the venue.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The Shadow Lines'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amitav Ghosh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'The Shadow Lines' ('द शैडो लाइन्स') is a novel written by Amitav Ghosh, published in 1988.

• The book won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1989.

• It explores themes of memory, nationalism, borders and the Partition of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Amitav Ghosh's other notable works include The Circle of Reason, The Glass Palace, The Hungry Tide and the Ibis Trilogy (Sea of Poppies, River of Smoke, Flood of Fire).

• He was awarded the Jnanpith Award (2018), the first English-language writer to receive it.

NOTE

• Hari Kunzru (Option 1): A British novelist, author of 'The Impressionist' and 'White Tears'.

• Pankaj Mishra (Option 3): An essayist and novelist, author of 'The Romantics' and 'Age of Anger'.

• Vikram Chandra (Option 4): Author of 'Sacred Games' and 'Red Earth and Pouring Rain'.

question: Which Hindi novel by Munshi Premchand depicts the life of Indian peasants?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Godan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Godan' (गोदान), written by Munshi Premchand in 1936, depicts the life and exploitation of Indian peasants (farmers) (भारतीय किसानों का जीवन).

• Its central character is the poor farmer Hori Mahato, whose lifelong dream is to own a cow.

• It is regarded as Premchand's greatest and last completed novel, a classic of Hindi and rural realism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Munshi Premchand (Dhanpat Rai Srivastava) is called the 'Upanyas Samrat' (Emperor of Novels).

• His other famous works include Gaban, Nirmala, Sevasadan, Rangbhoomi and the story Idgah.

NOTE

• Kurukshetra (Option 2): A famous Hindi poem by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, not by Premchand.

• Gunjan (Option 3): A poetry collection by Suryakant Tripathi 'Nirala', not a Premchand novel.

• Urvashi (Option 4): A Jnanpith-winning verse play by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar.

question: Jagannath Temple constructed by a famous king of Ganga Dynasty Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva dating back to 12th century is located at _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jagannath Temple (जगन्नाथ मंदिर) at Puri, Odisha was built in the 12th century by Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty.

• It is dedicated to Lord Jagannath (a form of Lord Vishnu/Krishna) and forms one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites.

• The temple is famous for its annual Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The temple is built in the Kalinga style of architecture.

• The Sun Temple at Konark, also in Odisha, was built by a later Ganga king, Narasimhadeva I.

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Known for the Khajuraho temples, not the Jagannath Temple.

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Home to Dravidian temples like Brihadeeswarar and Meenakshi, not Jagannath.

• Karnataka (Option 4): Known for Hoysala and Chalukya temples, not the Jagannath Temple.

question: 'Nagaur Fair' is held in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Nagaur Fair' (नागौर मेला) is held in the Nagaur district of Rajasthan (राजस्थान).

• It is one of India's largest cattle fairs, also known as the Ramdeoji Cattle Fair, famous for trading of bullocks, camels and horses.

• It is usually held in the month of January-February.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rajasthan hosts several famous fairs including the Pushkar Fair, Kolayat Fair and Kartik Fair.

• The Nagaur breed of bullocks (Nagauri) is prized for its work capacity.

NOTE

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Famous for fairs like the Kumbh Mela at Prayagraj, not Nagaur.

• Punjab (Option 3): Known for fairs like Maghi Mela and Hola Mohalla, not the Nagaur Fair.

• Bihar (Option 4): Hosts the Sonepur Cattle Fair, not the Nagaur Fair.

question: Where is the Hawa Mahal (having 953 windows) located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hawa Mahal (हवा महल), or 'Palace of Winds', having 953 windows (jharokhas), is located in Jaipur, Rajasthan.

• It was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh.

• It was designed by architect Lal Chand Ustad in the shape of the crown of Lord Krishna.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The structure is made of red and pink sandstone, giving Jaipur its 'Pink City' character.

• The many windows allowed royal ladies to observe street festivities while remaining unseen (purdah).

NOTE

• Ajmer (Option 2): Known for the Dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti and Ana Sagar Lake, not Hawa Mahal.

• Alwar (Option 3): Known for Bala Quila and Sariska Tiger Reserve, not Hawa Mahal.

• Sikar (Option 4): A Shekhawati region town famous for havelis, not the Hawa Mahal.

question: In West Bengal, the festival of Durga Puja starts with which of the following events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In West Bengal, the festival of Durga Puja begins with Mahalaya (महालय), which marks the arrival of Goddess Durga on Earth.

• Mahalaya falls on the last day of the dark fortnight (Amavasya) before the Navaratri and heralds the countdown to Durga Puja.

• It is traditionally marked by the recitation of 'Mahishasura Mardini' (Chandi Path) in the early morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The main days of Durga Puja are Shashthi, Saptami, Ashtami, Navami and Dashami (Vijaya Dashami).

• On Mahalaya, the eyes of the Durga idol are painted, a ritual known as 'Chokkhu Daan'.

NOTE

• Navami (Option 2): The ninth day of the festival, near its conclusion, not its beginning.

• Dasham/Dashami (Option 3): Vijaya Dashami, the last day marking the immersion of the idol.

• Poila Baishakh (Option 4): The Bengali New Year (April), unrelated to the start of Durga Puja.

question: 'Pandava' dance, performed during Dussehra and Diwali, belongs to which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Pandava' dance (पांडव नृत्य), performed during Dussehra and Diwali, belongs to the state of Uttarakhand, mainly the Garhwal region.

• Also called Pandav Nritya, it dramatizes episodes from the epic Mahabharata, especially the deeds of the Pandavas.

• Performers enter trance-like states while enacting the epic accompanied by dhol-damau drums.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Uttarakhand include Langvir Nritya, Barada Nati, Chholiya and Jhora.

• The dance is a devotional and community tradition celebrated over several days in Garhwal villages.

NOTE

• Assam (Option 1): Known for the Bihu dance, not the Pandava dance.

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Known for Lavani and Tamasha folk forms.

• Karnataka (Option 4): Known for Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha, not Pandava dance.

question: Which of the following Indian state practices the folk dance form 'Monyoasho'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The folk dance form 'Monyoasho' (मोन्योआशो) is practised in the state of Nagaland.

• It is associated with the Chakhesang Naga tribe and is performed during festivals and community celebrations.

• Naga folk dances are typically performed in traditional attire with rhythmic group movements and war-like postures.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nagaland's famous festival is the Hornbill Festival, held in December, showcasing tribal dances.

• Other Naga dances include the Zeliang dance, War dance and Modse.

NOTE

• Goa (Option 1): Known for Dekhni, Fugdi and Dhalo folk dances.

• Telangana (Option 2): Known for Perini Shivatandavam and Lambadi dances.

• West Bengal (Option 4): Known for Chhau, Gambhira and Baul traditions.

question: Why is hydrogen used as fuel in a cryogenic engine?
option_1: Because it is easy to store at room temperature.
option_3: Because it has the highest energy output per kilogram.
option_4: Because it is very cheap in comparison to other fuels.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because it has the highest energy output per kilogram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Hydrogen is used as fuel in a cryogenic engine (क्रायोजेनिक इंजन) because it has the highest energy output (calorific value) per kilogram of any fuel.

• In a cryogenic engine, liquid hydrogen (LH2) acts as the fuel and liquid oxygen (LOX) acts as the oxidiser, stored at extremely low temperatures.

• This high energy-to-weight ratio makes hydrogen ideal for rocket propulsion where minimising weight is crucial.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Liquid hydrogen must be stored below about -253°C and liquid oxygen below about -183°C.

• India's GSLV uses an indigenous cryogenic upper stage developed by ISRO.

NOTE

• Because it is easy to store at room temperature (Option 1): False; hydrogen must be liquefied at cryogenic temperatures, which is difficult.

• Because it is non-flammable (Option 2): False; hydrogen is highly flammable, which is why it works as a fuel.

• Because it is very cheap in comparison to other fuels (Option 4): False; producing and handling liquid hydrogen is expensive.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding Chandrayaan-1 mission?
I. It was the first lunar mission of India.
II. It confirmed the presence of water on the Moon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chandrayaan-1 (चंद्रयान-1) was India's first lunar mission, launched by ISRO on 22 October 2008 (Statement I correct).

• It confirmed the presence of water (in the form of hydroxyl / water molecules) on the Moon through its Moon Impact Probe and NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3) instrument (Statement II correct).

• Hence, both statements are correct (I और II दोनों).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chandrayaan-1 was launched using the PSLV-C11 rocket from Sriharikota.

• It carried 11 payloads, including instruments from ISRO, NASA, ESA and Bulgaria.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as Statement II is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as Statement I is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are true.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding fluid friction?
I. It is also called a drag.
II. It depends on the speed of the object with respect to the fluid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fluid friction (द्रव घर्षण) is the resistance experienced by an object moving through a fluid (liquid or gas), and it is also called drag (Statement I correct).

• The magnitude of fluid friction depends on the speed of the object relative to the fluid — it increases with speed (Statement II correct).

• Therefore, both statements are correct (I और II दोनों).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Fluid friction also depends on the shape of the object and the viscosity of the fluid.

• Streamlined shapes (like aircraft and fish) reduce fluid friction/drag.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, since Statement II is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, since Statement I is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are true.

question: Which institute received Rs. 4.2 crore funding in 2025 to develop next-gen digital forensic tools?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IIIT Pune and NIT Raipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2025, IIIT Pune and NIT Raipur jointly received Rs 4.2 crore in funding to develop next-generation digital forensic tools (डिजिटल फोरेंसिक उपकरण).

• The project aims to strengthen India's capabilities in cybercrime investigation and digital evidence analysis.

• Digital forensics involves recovering, analysing and preserving digital data as evidence for legal and security purposes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• IIIT stands for Indian Institute of Information Technology; NIT stands for National Institute of Technology.

• Such research supports national initiatives on cybersecurity and law enforcement.

NOTE

• IIT Bombay and IIT Guwahati (Option 1): Premier IITs, but not the recipients of this particular grant.

• IISc Bangalore and IIT Madras (Option 2): Leading research institutes, not associated with this funding.

• Delhi University and IIT Delhi (Option 3): Not the institutes that received this digital forensic grant.

question: The extraction of oil from groundnut is an example of economic activity of which sector of economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Secondary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The extraction (processing) of oil from groundnut is an example of the Secondary sector (द्वितीयक क्षेत्र) of the economy.

• The secondary sector involves manufacturing and processing — converting raw materials (groundnut) into finished/semi-finished goods (oil).

• Growing the groundnut is a primary activity, but processing it into oil is a secondary (industrial) activity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Primary sector covers agriculture, mining and other extraction of natural resources.

• The Tertiary sector covers services like transport, banking and trade.

NOTE

• Primary (Option 1): Involves natural resource extraction like farming and mining, not processing.

• Quaternary (Option 3): Knowledge-based services such as research and IT.

• Quinary (Option 4): High-level decision-making services (top executives, policymakers).

question: In the context of National Highways and Development Projects, what is the total length (in km) of East-West Corridor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3640.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP), the East-West Corridor (पूर्व-पश्चिम कॉरिडोर) has a total length of about 3,640 km.

• It connects Silchar (Assam) in the east to Porbandar (Gujarat) in the west.

• It is part of Phase II of the NHDP, along with the North-South Corridor.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The North-South Corridor (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) is about 4,000 km long.

• Together the two corridors form the NSEW Corridor, implemented by the NHAI.

NOTE

• 2900 (Option 1): Incorrect; understates the length of the East-West Corridor.

• 4700 (Option 3): Incorrect figure for the corridor's length.

• 5860 (Option 4): Far exceeds the actual length of about 3,640 km.

question: Why does the human heart has different chambers?
option_2: To pump blood to different organs
option_3: To prevent the mixing of oxygen-rich blood with carbon dioxide-rich blood
solution_text:
The correct answer is To prevent the mixing of oxygen-rich blood with carbon dioxide-rich blood.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The human heart has different chambers (अलग-अलग कोष्ठ) mainly to prevent the mixing of oxygen-rich (oxygenated) blood with carbon dioxide-rich (deoxygenated) blood.

• The human heart is four-chambered — two atria (upper) and two ventricles (lower).

• The right side handles deoxygenated blood and the left side handles oxygenated blood, keeping the two circulations separate (double circulation).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• This separation ensures efficient oxygen supply to body tissues and supports a high metabolic rate in warm-blooded animals.

• Valves between the chambers prevent the backflow of blood.

NOTE

• To regulate body temperature (Option 1): Temperature regulation is done by the skin, blood vessels and hypothalamus, not heart chambers.

• To pump blood to different organs (Option 2): Pumping is the heart's overall function, but the specific reason for separate chambers is to avoid mixing of blood.

• To store blood (Option 4): The heart pumps blood; it is not a storage organ (the spleen stores some blood).
